images.prompt:
Input image 1 is ONLY the approved visual style reference. Match its paper, palette, ink linework, subtle texture, typography, and spacing. Create a new subject, not a copy of its graph.
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: an editorial raster illustration for an adult statistics course, one of a consistent fifteen-image series. Style: a carefully art-directed human-designed university textbook illustration, restrained ink drawing and very subtle screen-print texture, crisp intentional geometry, a warm ivory paper background (#f8f5ee), dark graphite (#263849), muted ink blue (#285777), and a small ochre accent (#b4874b). Atmosphere: calm, thoughtful, trustworthy, uncluttered. Landscape 3:2 composition with generous negative space, a single central teaching diagram, balanced margins. Fine hand-ink character should be subtle; labels must be clean typeset sans-serif, not fake handwriting. No image headline, paragraph, footnote, decorative objects, stock icons, visual metaphors, gradients, 3D, glossy surfaces, glow, cartoon characters, gratuitous arrows, ornamental border, logo, or watermark. Use large sparse labels that remain legible when the image is displayed at 360 pixels wide. All diagram elements are schematic, not a claimed plot of observed data. No invented numerical data. Limit to at most four short labels. The scientific geometry and meaning are more important than decorative texture.
Primary request: Lesson 6: distinguish within-group spread from between-group mean differences. Draw one sparse diagram with THREE separated narrow vertical clusters of FOUR small blue dots each, no axes or numeric ticks. Put a short ochre horizontal mean mark across each cluster. Means are at modestly different heights, while dots have visibly larger within-group spread. A thin vertical bracket beside the first cluster points to its spread; a second understated bracket between two mean levels identifies mean separation. Exact labels, only "Within groups" and "Between means". No letter labels for groups, no test result, p-value, causal claim, numerical data, trend line, extra panels, or statistics formula. The three clusters must remain separate, and mean bars must sit within their respective clusters. This is a schematic explanation of two sources of variation, not the actual ANES result.

Primary request: Lesson 7: show that a group contrast changes across levels of another factor. Draw one simple two-line profile plot on sparse axes, no numbers or y-axis wording. X-axis endpoints have exact labels "Low" and "High". Blue and ochre lines each connect just TWO dots, at low and high. The blue line rises gently and the ochre line rises more steeply, so their separation clearly changes between low and high. Keep the two lines NONPARALLEL but NONCROSSING. Exact direct labels "Group A" and "Group B" at their right ends. Only these four labels. Do not add confidence bands, a legend, grid, p-values, formula, extra dots, or imply statistical significance. This is a schematic interaction pattern, not the ANES fitted result. Both groups share the same low/high axis.

A blue capped horizontal interval runs from left of zero to right of zero. Place one blue estimate dot LEFT of zero, inside the interval. Exact labels "Zero" beneath the dashed reference, "Estimate" above the dot, "Interval" below the blue capped segment.
